plan.notes: Sequence: official Department of Computer Science 'B.S. in Computer Science Four-Year Plan of Study' (csds.gsu.edu/b-s-in-computer-science-four-year-plan-of-study), live undated page captured 2026-09-30; the department notes it is 'one of many possible combinations of courses for students starting in MATH 1113.' Catalog_year 2024-2025 reflects the Undergraduate Catalog program page actually read and cross-verified (catalogs.gsu.edu, catoid=38, 'Computer Science, B.S.'); the live catalog as of collection is 2025-2026 (catoid=42) with the same program structure. Credits cross-verified against 2024-2025 catalog program pages, official GSU syllabi (math.gsu.edu; tinman.cs.gsu.edu), and the 2024-2025 Graduate Catalog CSC foundation list. Course-code note: the plan page writes 'ENG 1101/1102' but the official catalog registration code is ENGL 1101/1102 ('English Composition I/II'), used here. HIST 2210 is named on the plan (Area E) with no title published; its title is left descriptive rather than invented. Credit caveats: CSC 4351/4352 (2 hrs each), CSC 3350 (4), CSC 3320 (3) per the university-published B.S. curriculum transcription; CSC 3210 = 3 hrs per the current (2024-2025) Graduate Catalog foundation list (an older transcription listed 4). The four CSC 4xxx elective slots are 4 hrs each toward the catalog's 16-hour elective requirement ('at least four courses... at the 3000- or 4000-level'); individual electives vary, so confirm selections with an advisor. Placement: the plan assumes starting in MATH 1113; GSU recommends the math placement test for students without Area A math credit. Major eligibility (catalog): grade C or higher on first attempt in CSC 1301, CSC 2510 (or MATH 2420), and MATH 1113/2211/2212/2215, with a 2.5 average across them, is required to enroll in CSC 2720 and all 3000-/4000-level CSC courses; prereqs are strictly enforced. Prereq sources: CSC 2720 eligibility per catalog; CSC 3210 per official Summer 2024 syllabus (CSC 1302 and CSC 2510, or MATH 2420 in place of CSC 2510, C or better); MATH 3020 and MATH 2641 per official math.gsu.edu syllabi (MATH 2212 with C or higher); CSC 4351 per department news (passed CSC 4520, CSC 4320, or CSC 4330 — the latter two are the options of the CSC-OS-PL choice slot); CSC 4352 follows CSC 4351 in the two-semester capstone sequence. Calculus rollover: only 3 of each 4-credit calculus course's hours count in Areas A/D; the 4th 'rollover hour' counts in the Field of Study area (catalog). total_credits 120 = the term-by-term sequence sum and the published B.S. degree minimum.
